PullRequest.Title: Enable tool search for GPT-6 models
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- enable Copilot SDK tool search for the GPT-6 family, including Luna and Sol
- add regression coverage for GPT-6 and Claude Opus 5.5 routing
- replace Opus 4.8 with Opus 5 and Opus 5.5 in the Agent Host prompt snapshot matrix
- refresh the Opus 5 prompt baseline and record the new Opus 5.5 capture/baseline

## Validation

- focused tool-search unit tests (9 passing)
- prompt snapshot formatting tests (2 passing)
- Opus 5 prompt replay (1 passing)
- Opus 5.5 prompt recording and replay (1 passing each)
- ESLint on the five changed TypeScript files

Scenarios.Scenario: Launch or resume an Agent Host coding session using a GPT-6-family model with the default tool-search setting and the client toolSearch tool available
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Launch configuration filters the tool snapshot, evaluates the changed GPT-6 model predicate, constructs SDK tools with defer metadata, then creates/resumes the SDK session and sends the first model request. The predicate and tool-array mapping are synchronous local work; the model request is the expensive critical-path boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/resume the SDK session and send the model request containing the active and deferred tool projection
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One session create/resume request, followed by the normal per-turn model requests; tool schemas scale with the registered tool set but are deferred rather than eagerly exposed for GPT-6 after the change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: GPT-6 failed the support predicate, so the same existing model request eagerly exposed non-core client/MCP tool definitions instead of marking them for on-demand discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The initial model request must complete before the session can respond. The diff changes its tool projection for GPT-6 but does not add another launch-time boundary call.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number and schema size of registered client/MCP tools. Tool search replaces eager inclusion of non-core tool definitions with defer metadata; the changed model check itself is O(model-id length).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One launch/resume configuration is built per session operation. Tool construction is synchronous and no new parallel fan-out or limiter is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new application cache or retained key set is introduced. Provider prompt caching may benefit from a smaller/stabler request, but that is outside the changed code and not required for the verdict.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed predicate reaches toolSearchActive, createClientSdkTools, and the SDK toolSearch option directly, and repository tests/documentation establish deferThreshold=1 behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact token and latency savings depend on each user's installed MCP/client tool set and provider behavior; this affects benefit magnitude, not the traced mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff extends an existing payload-bounding mechanism to GPT-6 and adds no launch-time boundary fan-out, unbounded retention, or repeated work.

Scenarios.Scenario: A GPT-6 coding turn needs a deferred MCP or non-core VS Code tool
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The model first invokes tool_search_tool; Agent Host forwards one ready action with the deferred candidate corpus to the workbench, the workbench invokes the existing toolSearch client tool, returns its result, and the model then selects/invokes the desired tool. These steps are serialized and lie on the turn critical path only when the model chooses tool search.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forward the tool-search call and candidate metadata from Agent Host to the workbench, then return the tool result
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC-style client-tool interaction per tool_search_tool invocation, carrying one grouped candidate list; not one call per candidate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: For GPT-6 specifically, tool search was inactive, so the model received all tool schemas up front and could invoke the desired tool directly without this discovery interaction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks discovery of the selected deferred tool for that turn.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: Copilot SDK/provider turn continuation reached from the Agent Host session
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Continue the model turn after the tool-search result so the model can invoke a discovered tool
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional serialized continuation per model-selected search invocation; no candidate-level fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: GPT-6 turns had no tool-search continuation because schemas were eagerly available in the model request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds an on-demand round trip before a deferred tool can execute, while avoiding eager transfer/processing of every deferred schema on the initial request.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective candidate cardinality is the set of tools marked deferLoading after SDK grouping/filtering. Candidate metadata is copied once per model-selected search invocation, not once per candidate boundary call.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Search and selected-tool execution are sequential for the demonstrated workflow. There is no changed Promise.all, burst, queue, or per-candidate IPC fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no code-level result cache or coalescing on this path; repeated searches are model-selected invocations. Warm sessions reuse the established session but do not cache search results in the reviewed code.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the runtime implementation and end-to-end test establish exactly one search client-tool call followed by the selected tool, with candidate metadata grouped into that call.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: How often GPT-6 selects deferred tools, the installed tool count, provider round-trip latency, and net latency versus reduced prompt processing are workload-dependent.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable performance bug. The extra serialized discovery boundary is the intentional on-demand side of deferred loading, is bounded per model-selected search invocation rather than per candidate, and is offset by removing eager schema payload from every request. No evidence shows an accidental repeat, fan-out, concurrency burst, or cache/lifecycle defect.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run or record the Claude Opus 5.5 prompt E2E matrix
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The test harness substitutes Opus 5.5 for Opus 4.8 in a fixed model list, constructs one prompt snapshot for that model, and uses the existing capture/provider request path. This is test-only and off the product runtime path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recorded/replayed provider exchange in the E2E harness
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One model case replaces one previous case in the fixed matrix.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same matrix slot and capture path ran for Claude Opus 4.8.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Affects only the selected E2E test case, not product startup or interaction latency.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed snapshot-model matrix cardinality; the PR replaces one entry rather than increasing the number of models.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Unchanged test-runner scheduling; no new parallel work is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Static capture and snapshot fixtures replace prior files; no runtime cache keys or retained state change.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all relevant changes are model-id substitutions and generated snapshot updates with unchanged matrix cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for product performance; fixture text size changes only repository/test I/O by a bounded amount.
Scenarios.Verdict: No product performance regression and no meaningful test-suite scaling regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 25 changed files and every diff page. Traced GPT-6 model matching through launch configuration, deferred SDK tool construction, tool-search IPC, workbench invocation, and provider continuation. The change intentionally bounds eager tool-schema payloads; its on-demand discovery cost is serialized and grouped, with no diff-introduced unbounded retention, per-candidate fan-out, concurrency burst, or repeated hot-path work. No findings were submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
